claude.result:
`langsmith.ts` sends Claude Code sessions to LangSmith as traces. It takes conversation turns that have already been parsed, turns each one into a tree of LangSmith runs (a turn, the LLM calls inside it, their tool calls, and any subagents or workflows), and submits them through the LangSmith JS SDK. It appears to be driven by Claude Code hooks: runs are opened, patched and flushed as hook events arrive.

I didn't read the file myself. It's 1,227 lines, so a smaller model (Haiku) read it and this summary is based on its answer. The line numbers are its citations.

## Setup and teardown
- **`initTracing`** (L32): creates the shared LangSmith client. It also sets up replicas (extra destinations the same traces are sent to) and optional redaction, with extra redaction rules if given.
- **`flushPendingTraces`** (L56): sends any batched runs before the hook process exits.

## Run ordering
- **`generateDottedOrderSegment`** (L76) and **`parseDottedOrder`** (L99) build and parse LangSmith's `dotted_order` string, which has the form `<timestamp><runId>.<timestamp><runId>…`. This string is what places each run correctly in the tree.

## Tracing a turn (the core)
- **`traceTurn`** (L188), configured through `TraceTurnOptions` (L161):
  - It creates a root Turn run of type chain, or nests under a parent run it's given.
  - For each LLM call it posts an `llm` run, then a run for each tool call. Messages build up across calls so each LLM run has the full context.
  - It records every Agent or Task tool run in a `taskRunMap` (entry type `TaskRunEntry`, L806), keyed by agent ID. This map is returned so that subagents can later be attached under the tool call that started them.
  - It supports two tracing modes, `"full"` and `"metadata"`, set per turn and per tool. It also stamps custom metadata, runtime version, approval policy and agent type onto the runs.

## Subagents and workflows
- **`tracePendingSubagents`** (L828) handles subagents that the `SubagentStop` hook queued (`PendingSubagent`, L799):
  - It reads each subagent's transcript, splits it into turns, and fills in the deferred Agent tool run with the real subagent name.
  - It then calls the internal `traceSubagentChain`, which creates a chain run under the Agent run and calls `traceTurn` again for each of the subagent's turns.
- **`traceWorkflowStage`** (L1089) uses `traceSubagentChain` the same way to trace one stage of a dynamic workflow under the Workflow tool run.
- **`closeAgentToolRun`** (L1154) closes an Agent tool run that `tracePendingSubagents` left open. This is for async subagents that finish later.

## Closing turns
- **`completeTurnRun`** (L605) closes the root Turn run with the final assistant output. **`closeTurnRun`** (L626) force-closes it with an error or status. Both go through an internal `patchTurnRun` and identify the turn with `TurnRunIdentity` (L514), which **`turnIdentityFromOpenTurn`** (L578) rebuilds from the stored open-turn state.
- **`closeInterruptedTurn`** (L643) recovers from a user interrupt. It traces any LLM calls still pending from the transcript, runs `tracePendingSubagents`, and closes the turn with a "User interrupt" error.

## How they fit together
`initTracing` runs first. Then `traceTurn` handles each turn and returns the `taskRunMap` of Agent and Workflow tool runs. When subagents or workflow stages finish, `tracePendingSubagents` and `traceWorkflowStage` hang their own turn trees off the matching entries in that map. A turn is then closed by `completeTurnRun`, `closeTurnRun` or `closeInterruptedTurn`, with `closeAgentToolRun` closing any async Agent runs later. `flushPendingTraces` runs last, before the process exits. The dotted-order helpers are used throughout to keep the parent/child structure intact while all of this is spread over separate hook calls.
